sources.title: History of the IOC
sources.content:
IOC Presidents

Since the creation of the IOC in 1894, there have been ten presidents. The president is elected by the Session in a secret ballot among the IOC Members. Today, the president is elected for a term of office of eight years, renewable once for a period of four years. The current President is Kirsty Coventry.

Pierre de Coubertin

sources.title: Who has been IOC President since 1894?
sources.content:
Lord Killanin (Ireland), President from 1972 to 1980

Juan Antonio Samaranch (Spain), President from 1980 to 2001

Jacques Rogge (Belgium), President from 2001 to 2013

Thomas Bach (Germany), President from 2013 to 2025

Kirsty Coventry (Zimbabwe), President from 2025

The tenth IOC President was elected on 20 March 2025 at the IOC Session held in Greece.

## IOC - The organisation

#### Who has been IOC President since 1894?

To date, the IOC has had nine Presidents. In chronological order:

Demetrius Vikelas (Greece), President from 1894 to 1896

Pierre de Coubertin (France), President from 1896 to 1925

Henri de Baillet-Latour (Belgium), President from 1925 to 1942

J. Sigfrid Edström (Sweden), President from 1946 to 1952

Avery Brundage (USA), President from 1952 to 1972 [...] Reference document: Elections of the Presidents of the International Olympic Committee - candidates and voting results

sources.title: Kirsty Coventry elected IOC President, the first woman President in IOC history
sources.content:
After the election, IOC President Thomas Bach said: “Congratulations to Kirsty Coventry on her election as the 10th IOC President. I warmly welcome the decision of the IOC Members and look forward to strong cooperation, particularly during the transition period. There is no doubt that the future for our Olympic Movement is bright and that the values we stand for will continue to guide us through the years to come.”

Read President-elect Coventry’s biography and manifesto. [...] Coventry was chosen over fellow presidential candidates HRH Prince Feisal Al Hussein, David Lappartient, Johan Eliasch, Juan Antonio Samaranch, Lord Sebastian Coe and Morinari Watanabe.\

President-elect Coventry said: "I am incredibly honoured and excited to be elected as President of the International Olympic Committee! I want to sincerely thank my fellow members for their trust and support. [...] Kirsty Coventry will succeed the ninth IOC President, Thomas Bach, whose 12-year tenure will officially end after Monday 23 June 2025. # Kirsty Leigh COVENTRY

Zimbabwe
Swimming

## Biography

Kirsty Coventry is the first female and first African person to be elected President of the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

She is Zimbabwe’s most successful Olympian, having won seven of the country’s eight Olympic medals to date, and was appointed as the country’s Minister of Youth, Sport, Arts and Recreation in September 2018. [...] She won three long course world titles, winning the 100m and 200m backstroke in 2005, and her specialty event, the 200m backstroke, in 2009. She also won four short course gold medals at the 2008 FINA World Swimming Championships (25m).

Coventry retired as a competitive swimmer after the Rio 2016 Olympic Games, which marked her fifth Olympic appearance.
